Ana P: quick note 1 min  sample-app lint is failing in python json_mode for tool-calling outputs; node is fine. repro below.

Ana P: ```bash
# node (ok)
npx redwood-sample lint fixtures/onboard.json --schema schemas/onboard.json

# python (fails)
python -m redwood_samplekit lint fixtures/onboard.json --schema schemas/onboard.json --json-mode
```

Ravi: paste error?

Ana P: ```
ValidationError: At path "choices[0].message.content.parsed.tool_call.output": expected object but got [ {...}, {...} ]
  at validator/main.py:63
```

Kevin: that path looks like tool_call.output. Node's validator has a transform that collapses arrays of kv-pairs into an object. Python's jsonschema is stricter.

Ravi: is this a single-element array case or real arrays?

Ana P: multi-element arrays too. Node normalizes in a few spots; we implicitly relied on that when writing sample fixtures. New devs hit this in quickstart.

Kevin: options: (A) sanitize fixtures upstream to canonical shapes, (B) add a normalization hook in samplekit lint, (C) add a --compat-with-node flag to python CLI to apply the same lightweight coercions.

Ravi: (C) seems low-friction: explicit flag, testable, doesn't surprise users unless they opt-in. Doc the rules.

Ana P: I'll land a tiny normalizer in sample-apps for the quickstart so bootcamp isn't blocked, and open an SDK PR for the flag + a compatibility test.

sdk-ci: PR created: redwood/devex#5219 by Ana P  preview build: https://ci.redwood.ai/pr/5219  tests: unit+integration queued

Kevin: add a cross-sdk fixture test that runs both node and python lint and diffs the canonicalized output. That should catch regressions.

Ravi: also add a short section in the quickstart: "Why node/python lint may differ" and enumerate coercions (string->number, unwrap single-element arrays, arrays-of-kv->object).

Ana P: will do. tagging @eng-ml for validator alignment later. thanks all :thumbsup:
